reason: The quote states Object Lock works only in buckets with S3 Versioning enabled, that a retention period or legal hold protects only the version specified in the request, and that locks do not prevent new versions or delete markers.

Under Retention periods the quotes state you can extend a retention period with a new request carrying a later Retain Until Date, S3 replaces it with the longer period, and setting one needs s3:PutObjectRetention.
The quote states the minimum and maximum allowable retention periods can be restricted with the s3:object-lock-remaining-retention-days condition key in the bucket policy.
The quote states a unique retention period can be set for individual objects and a default retention period can be set on an S3 bucket.

The quotes name the two ways (retention periods and legal holds), say a version can have either or both, a retention period is a fixed period, and a legal hold has no expiration date and stays until removed.
The quote says Object Lock can help prevent deletion or overwrite; the claim drops the hedge and states it prevents them, which overstates the quote (governance mode can be bypassed).
The quote states Object Lock stores objects with a WORM model, can help prevent accidental or inappropriate deletion, and gives protecting CloudTrail logs as the example.
The objects overview says each object can be up to 50 TB, and the document history row dated December 2, 2025 says the maximum object size increased from 5 TB to 50 TB.
The quote states documentation commonly references 50 TB but the actual maximum is 53.7 TB (48.8 TiB), set by 10,000 parts x 5 GiB per part.

The quote states Object Ownership is a bucket-level setting, defaults to Bucket owner enforced with all ACLs disabled, and the bucket owner then owns all objects and manages access only with policies.
The context says ACLs can be disabled on new and existing buckets; the quote says on an existing bucket ACLs leave access evaluation, policies decide, and re-enabling restores the preexisting ACLs.
The quote states that with ACLs disabled the bucket accepts only PUTs without an ACL or with bucket-owner-full-control, and other ACLs fail with a 400 error AccessControlListNotSupported.
The three quotes define Bucket owner enforced (default), Bucket owner preferred with the bucket-owner-full-control canned ACL, and Object writer exactly as the claim states.
The quote states objects consist of data and metadata, metadata is name-value pairs including date last modified and Content-Type, and custom metadata can be set when the object is stored.
The decision-guide quote states object storage is accessed through an API over the internet and is well-suited to read-heavy workloads such as streaming.
The quote states S3 is an object storage service storing data within buckets, an object is a file and any metadata, and a bucket is a container for objects.
The quotas table row under Name/Default/Adjustable/Description gives Object tags 10, not adjustable, the maximum number of tags per S3 object.
The FAQ quote states tags are key-value pairs created, updated or deleted any time, used for IAM policies, Lifecycle policies and storage metrics, and can drive transitions and expiration.

The quote frames writer ownership as the default behaviour, not as a condition of ACLs being in use; the claim replaces that with 'when ACLs are in use', which the quote does not say and which is wrong under Bucket owner preferred with bucket-owner-full-control.
The quote states objects stored in a Region never leave it unless you explicitly transfer or replicate them to another Region.

The quotes and context state One Zone-IA uses one AZ, is as durable as Standard-IA but less available, is not resilient to physical AZ loss, and is recommended for re-creatable data such as CRR replicas.
The quote states other classes use a minimum of three AZs while One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ and costs 20% less than S3 Standard-IA.
The quote states aggressive timeouts and retries help drive consistent latency because a retried request is likely to take a different path and quickly succeed.
The quote recommends accessing the bucket from EC2 instances in the same Region when possible to reduce network latency and data transfer costs.
The quote states best performance comes from multiple concurrent requests over separate connections and S3 has no limit on connections to a bucket.
The quote states a resource owner can grant permissions to another account, which can delegate them or a subset to its users, but cannot delegate them cross-account to another AWS account.
The quote states access not explicitly allowed is implicitly denied and an explicit deny keeps a user out even if a different policy grants access.
The quote and its context give the bucket-level ARN, bucket_name/* for all objects and bucket_name/prefix/* for a prefix; the second quote says s3:ListBucket allows ListObjectsV2.
The quote states a prefix is a string at the beginning of the key name, organizes data like directories, but prefixes are not directories.
The quote gives the example of 10 prefixes parallelizing reads to scale to 55,000 read requests per second; the claim keeps it framed as an example.
The quote states at least 3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE or 5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second per partitioned prefix; the qualifiers keep 'at least' and gradual scaling.
The quotes state there are no limits to the number of prefixes in a bucket and that writes (and, in context, reads) scale by using multiple prefixes.
The quotes state CLI or SDK presigned URLs can be set as high as 7 days from creation, and IAM user credentials are valid up to 7 days with Signature Version 4.
The quotes state a console presigned URL can be set between 1 minute and 12 hours, with 12 hours from creation as the maximum.
The quote states the S3 console can generate a presigned URL for sharing an object up to 5 TB.
The quote states presigned URLs made with EC2 instance role credentials are valid for the duration of the role credentials, typically 6 hours.

The quotes state anyone with valid credentials can create a presigned URL, access succeeds only if the creator has permission for the operation, and capabilities are limited by the creator's permissions; bearer tokens is verbatim.
The quotes state a URL made with a temporary credential expires when the credential expires even with a later expiration time, whichever occurs first, and with AssumeRole when the role session ends.

The quotes state aws:SourceIp for the public endpoint, aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceVpce for a VPC endpoint, set on the principal or the bucket/access point, and that the restrictions also apply outside presigned URLs.
The quotes state a presigned URL can be used multiple times up to its expiration, and S3 checks expiration at request time so a download started before expiry continues.
